flawed_step: 0006-0009: the asserted equivalence omits the enumerated element j_0 because the series begins at n=1.
counterexample: Let V=R, I=J={0,1,2,...}, and j_n=n. Set v_0=1 and v_n=0 for every n>=1, and take r=1. The support {0} is contained in J. The generalized sum over J converges absolutely to 1, since sum_{j in J}|v_j|=1 and sum_{j in J}v_j=1. But the displayed series sum_{n=1}^infinity v_{j_n} has every term equal to 0, so it converges absolutely to 0, not to r=1. Thus the equivalence in lines 0006-0009 is false.
assessment_summary: Lines 0001-0004 correctly restrict the generalized sum to J because all terms outside J vanish. The next equivalence fails due to an indexing mismatch: the enumeration starts with j_0, while the series starts at n=1 and therefore need not include v_{j_0}.
